liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **He's Gone** (3 reviews): Attendee remembers it as a tribute to John Lennon; Reviewer says tears ran down Jerry's face during it, then the band rocked out [13][17][22]
- **I Know You Rider** (2 reviews): Listener overheated in the general admission front and passed out around this song, then came back dancing [11][12]
- **Althea** (1 review): The first-set version is extremely good [15]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): China>Rider has unfamiliar meandering jams alongside the traditional wallop [15]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Reviewer calls it a standout version, with a great Jerry solo and an exploratory jam after the verses [15]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): Attendee recalls wailing playing in this song, part of a set of aural hallucinations [13]
- **Around and Around** (1 review): Jerry lifted a usually unloved Around and Around to a cooking level that had the hall rocking [21]
- **Peggy-O** (1 review): Jerry tuned into the somber mood on this song [21]

## Setlist highlights

- **Peggio**: back after 369 archived shows (2005 days); mythic rare: 2 archived performances [23]
- **(a foot gets tangled in the right channel mic cable - dual left channel from 1:57 to 3:07)**: back after 322 archived shows (1532 days) [23]
- **I Know You Rider**: with Mountain Jam tease [23]
- **Drum Break**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 3 archived performances [23]
- **Drum Break (continued)**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 3 archived performances [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-12-12.124542.aud.goldshine.sennheiser-mkh406-flyingm.flac16** (recommended): audience recording; 25 songs; 170 min; rated 4.56/5 by 18 [1]
- **gd1980-12-12.175120.sbd.miller.remaster.31509.flac1644**: soundboard; 23 songs; 173 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [3]
- **gd80-12-12.sbd.miller.31509.sbeok.flacf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 174 min; rated 3.6/5 by 10 [4]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sound quality is poor enough to limit listening; the audience recording is better; Soundboard is several generations removed from the original, with occasional bass distortion, but still clear and listenable [18][20]
- **gd1980-12-12.175907.nak700.ellner.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 23 songs; 173 min [5]
- **gd1980-12-12.fob.ellner.motb.89347.flac24**: source not stated; 22 songs; 167 min; rated 4.83/5 by 6 [7]
- **gd80-12-12.set1-aud.vernon.16906.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 11 songs; 67 min; rated 4.6/5 by 5 [10]. Said about its sound: The audience recording of the first set sounds decent [19]

## Around the show

- Guests: Mountain Jam tease [1]
- Reviewer says it was the last time the band played the Swing [11]
- Reviewer says it was the last time the band played the Swing [12]
- Attendee says the Swing was demolished rather than burned, and the Stones, Janis and Jimi played there [13]
- Said to be the band's first show after John Lennon was shot [17]
- Reviewer notes this was the band's last show at Swing Auditorium [19]
- First show after John Lennon's murder; San Bernardino sheriffs were out in force and the mood was somber [21]
- Reviewer recalls Airto Moreira and Flora Purim on stage at some point [22]
- Reviewer says this was the last concert at the Swing before it burned down; odd decorations hung from the ceiling [22]
- Reviewer rates it almost as good as '77 and better than '78, when Jerry was sick [11]
- Reviewer rates it almost as good as '77 and better than '78, when Jerry was sick [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-12-12.124542.aud.goldshine.sennheiser-mkh406-flyingm.flac16**: taped by Ron Goldshine and John Musgrave with help from Mark the B-Man and Mike Martin (guarding the mic stands); transferred by Mike Martin; source: Source: 2 Sennheiser MKH 406 TUD microphones > Sony D5M (w/ Dolby B, Bias @ 70us on 3 TDK MA C-90 tapes); Copy of masters: Sony D5M (w/ Dolby, Bias @ 70us) >… [1]. Also: Audience recording captured with Sennheiser MKH406 microphones [1]
- **gd1980-12-12.175120.sbd.miller.remaster.31509.flac1644**: transferred by Transfer and Remastering by Charlie Miller  November 14, 2025; source: SBD > Cassette (Nakamichi CR-7A) > DAT (Sony PCM-R500) [3]. Also: Soundboard remaster repairs a vocal phase issue, repatches tape flips, and fixes pitch and levels; Mike Shoun's tapes were transferred by Neil Sturtevant [3]
- **gd80-12-12.sbd.miller.31509.sbeok.flacf**: transferred by Neil Sturtevant and Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard [4]
- **gd1980-12-12.175907.nak700.ellner.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Ron Ellner; transferred by Bob Menke, Charlie Miller, Scott Clugston; source: Ron Ellner's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Nakamichi 550 (TDK MA C-90) through the tape flip in "Good Lovin'" Ron Ellner's Master (FOB)… [5]. Also: Bob Menke supplied master cassettes and first-generation reel transfers; A Sennheiser MKH406 source patches 12 seconds of Drums and 38 seconds of Good Lovin' [5]
- **gd1980-12-12.fob.ellner.motb.89347.flac24**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by A. Egert and SIRMick; source: 2 x Nakamichi CM-700 => Nakamichi 550 >> MAC [7]. Also: Right channel gain was reduced slightly; dropouts and clicks were repaired, and crossfades were added where the tape paused; The Drums tape flip was crossfaded without a patch; This transfer is missing the Don't Ease Me In encore [7]
- **gd80-12-12.set1-aud.vernon.16906.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [10]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Colby Poster: [Grateful Dead Swing Auditorium 1980 Cardboard Boxing-Style Poster](https://concertposterauction.com/Listing/Details/1302338/Grateful-Dead-Swing-Auditorium-1980-Cardboard-BoxingStyle-Poster) [24]
